        ### Question
        Question linked to image # 8 In relation to the previous case, how would you approach the initial treatment of this patient?

        ### Options
        opa. The treatment is the use of allopurinol at a minimum dose of 800 mg daily, so the dose used by the patient should be increased early.
opb. During the acute phase, the treatment is NSAIDs, which can be associated with colchicine.
opc. Given the severity of the lesions, intravenous colchicine should be used.
opd. If synovial fluid has a cell count above 3000 cells / μl, treatment with parenteral antibiotics should be initiated with coverage against Staphylococcus Aureus and Streptococcus spp. And maintained at least 6 weeks.
ope. In this disease, systemic or intraarticular steroids have not proven their efficacy.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Acute gout attack -> inflammation of joints -> pain and swelling -> 80% CHAIN: NSAIDs -> reduce inflammation and pain -> commonly used in acute gout -> 85% CHAIN: Colchicine -> inhibits inflammation -> effective in acute gout -> 80% CHAIN: Intravenous colchicine -> rapid onset of action -> used in severe cases -> 75% CHAIN: Synovial fluid cell count > 3000 cells/μl -> possible infection -> consider parenteral antibiotics -> 70% CHAIN: Systemic or intraarticular steroids -> not effective in gout -> not recommended -> 80%
